original_decision: When an archival conversion removes a forbidden action, promote its surviving Next subtree into its position; where the holder accepts only one action, retain the first survivor and attach the remaining sequence to its Next.
reason: This follows Table 196's required post-action sequence and Note 1's recursive order. The archival rewrite preserves the permitted actions after a removed Launch instead of losing them. Current source implements promotion and the integration test checks that a Named NextPage action remains after Launch removal.
current_code_evidence: crates/pdf-transform/src/archive/actions.rs::flatten and rewrite/promotion paths; crates/pdf-transform/tests/archive.rs::a_launch_action_goes_and_the_actions_behind_it_stay
test_evidence: The test converts a valid generated source, checks the unauthorized case writes nothing, then authorizes the action loss and confirms the forbidden Launch is removed while NextPage remains, with a conforming output and one removal report. This is a writer-side preservation test; reader action order is separately tested in action.rs. Parent correction: the test only searches output bytes for NextPage; it does NOT verify that OpenAction reaches it, nor ordering of multiple survivors. Meaningful preservation proof remains missing.
spec_or_external_sources: Effective EC3 §12.6.2 Table 196 /Next and Note 1; ISO 19005-2 6.5.1 and ISO 19005-4 6.6.1 as stated in ADR 1175.
changed_premise: No change found to the archive-removal premise or ordered /Next requirement. This review does not expand into all nine archive rewrite types in ADR 1175.
remaining_work: Followup archive_action_promotion_audit now supplies passing parsed reachability/order and shared-tail refusal tests; broader population remains partial.

original_decision: Refuse conversion when a shared action object is reached from distinct positions whose removals require different Next tails, rather than cloning or choosing one tail.
reason: The archive writer cannot represent two distinct successor sequences in one shared dictionary without changing identity or structure. However, the reader's global visited set independently deduplicates all repeated references, including non-cyclic siblings. Table 196 does not explicitly define the execution multiplicity of a repeated object reference; the sibling occurrence test draft probes this reader issue and does not invalidate the archive writer refusal rationale. Parent: conflicting tails refusal is a conservative project preservation choice; cloning could represent both sequences technically, so inability is conditional on the no-cloning fence rather than a PDF-format impossibility.
current_code_evidence: crates/pdf-transform/src/archive/actions.rs records one Next per object and refuses conflicting tails; crates/pdf-model/src/action.rs::push uses a global BTreeSet<ObjectId>.
test_evidence: Archive test a_launch_action_goes_and_the_actions_behind_it_stay covers promotion but not conflicting shared tails. Scratch tests.rs has a full valid-PDF positive control and repeated-reference discriminator; not run in this audit. Parent repeated-reference regression executed and FAILS; reader occurrence loss is separate from writer policy.
spec_or_external_sources: Effective EC3 §12.6.2 Table 196 and Note 1 distinguish ordered array execution from self-referential-cycle handling.
changed_premise: Reader implementation behavior now makes the shared-reference multiplicity question visible; it does not change the writer's inability to give one object two different tails.
remaining_work: Followup archive_action_promotion_audit now supplies passing parsed reachability/order and shared-tail refusal tests; broader population remains partial.

original_decision: Treat the one-page viewer's page-visible and page-open events as coincident, and page-invisible/page-close likewise; suppress a recursively cascading page-event loop with the existing raising guard.
reason: Co-raising PV/PI with page open/close is supported only for a single visible page. Current continuous and two-page layouts invalidate that general premise. ADR1750/1752 explicitly retain the neighbor-visibility limitation. Keep the recursion guard as a separate bounded policy, not a clause requirement.
current_code_evidence: crates/viewer-core/src/viewer/layout.rs places multiple pages; navigation.rs::page_events follows current index only.
test_evidence: Existing single-page ordered trace and new flags test pass but cannot prove visible-set transitions. Separate page_visibility_triggers_audit drafts test placed neighbors.
spec_or_external_sources: Effective EC3 §12.6.3 introductory discussion and Tables 197-198; the text explicitly distinguishes open from visible when more than one page may be visible and does not prescribe recursive-cascade prevention.
changed_premise: Multiple-page layouts already exist; the original single-page premise cannot justify all current layouts.
remaining_work: Track actual visible-set transitions separately from open/close; independently test recursion bounds. No production change in this audit.

Script timing tests do not establish handling of that action form. This finding is limited to the trigger consumer; it does not re-audit JavaScript realm policy.

'Addressed to this program' must now be read against the expanded program: it reads, transforms, assembles, and writes selected PDF structures. A clause can impose writer obligations on those operations even though authoring new page content remains excluded. Thus a viewer-only reading of the rule is stale; applicability is row- and operation-specific.

The current nine departed rows span reader, transformation, redaction, and writing operations.

original_decision: Retain the decoded prefix of a damaged page content stream when it consists of completed drawing instructions, and report the shortfall.
reason: Retaining a completed-instruction prefix with a damage report remains a deliberate recovery policy for page content streams. The prior premise that the decoded prefix's marks are additive or a subset of the complete stream's final picture is false: later opaque painting can erase earlier marks, and transparency, knockout, or soft-mask transfer can change prior contributions. Corrupt compressed bytes can also yield altered decoded bytes before failure, so consumed bits do not prove original producer bytes. These limits weaken the old rationale but do not require removing the recovery policy.
current_code_evidence: content/reader.rs and run.rs preserve decoded/windowed instruction prefixes; nested content uses the shared NestedContent runner.
test_evidence: leftover/damaged-content tests assert drawing plus damage reports; existing cases do not establish a subset relation to a valid complete stream. No Cargo run was performed. A separate optional scratch observation can compare black-prefix versus complete black-then-white painting; it is explanatory, not a conformance test.
spec_or_external_sources: ISO 32000-2 §§7.4.1, 7.8.2; ADR 0356 for the non-content-stream counterexample.
changed_premise: ADR 0359 expressly extended the original page-only decision to the other named content streams and distinguished CMap/sample data.
remaining_work: Keep prefix recovery explicitly labeled reader policy, not semantic equivalence or proof of producer bytes. Parent may add a standalone scratch observation comparing a truncated black rectangle with the complete black-then-white stream. Do not claim consumed bits prove original source bytes.

Later opaque paint, transparency, knockout, or soft-mask transfer can alter earlier contributions; damaged compressed data may also decode into altered bytes before the decoder detects failure. Retain prefix recovery as a deliberate reader policy and keep it limited to content instruction streams, without claiming semantic subset equivalence.

original_decision: viewer-core owns the five Table 200 calls: WC before close, WS before save serialization, DS after a successful write, WP when a granted print starts, and DP when an active print ends.
reason: Current call paths support the stated ordering. Close runs WillClose and emits its report before removing the document and emitting Closed. Save runs WillSave before XFA preSave and before serialization; DidSave follows only an Ok write. Print runs WillPrint only once policy/fidelity grants the job and DidPrint only when an active job is finished. A later XFA preSave event may cause the reader-level save policy to hold or refuse the write after WS, so WS is before an attempted save path and does not guarantee a file is written. That XFA condition is separate from Table 200 JavaScript event.rc.

original_decision: Cache a loaded font by its defining dictionary's object identity, not by the resource-name text, because a page and Form can reuse /F1 for distinct fonts.
reason: Current resolution first selects the entry from the active resource dictionary, then derives FontKey::Referenced from that entry's ObjectId. A name-keyed cache would conflate distinct dictionaries, while the current key distinguishes them. The resource-scope principle remains effective in §7.8.3 and the Type 3 glyph dispatch is a useful direct visible witness because glyph streams are self-contained vector programs and require no platform font substitution.
current_code_evidence: content/font.rs::Interpreter::font resolves the active `resources` argument's Font category, maps a reference to FontKey::Referenced(id), and asks/loads with that key. content/xobject.rs::form selects the Form's own Resources dictionary (legacy omission fallback is not exercised); run/nested.rs runs the nested stream with that dictionary and its caller resumes afterward. Type 3 loading returns Font::Type3 from the referenced dictionary; text/show dispatches its encoded codes through that font's CharProcs.
test_evidence: Existing text_render_modes.rs::a_forms_font_resource_is_not_the_pages asserts that a missing form /F1 is reported and only the page glyph draws; it does not test two defined same-named entries. type3_spec_audit.rs::a_d0_glyph_does_not_change_the_callers_graphics_state checks colored d0 state restoration with one Type 3 dictionary. The new draft supplies a complete PDF with red page font, blue Form font and a red page-font show after the Form; it asserts exact red/blue/red fills. Rustfmt passes; no Cargo/test run.
spec_or_external_sources: ISO 32000-2 §7.8.3, §8.10.1, and §9.6.4 at doc/md/ISO_32000-2_sponsored_EC3.md:3302-3325, 7764-7815; EC3 Issue #128 only changes Type 3 glyph resource lookup order, which this no-external-resource fixture does not exercise.

remaining_work: Parent review and, if accepted, promote the draft into a test target and run it. A mutation that changes the cache key back to resource-name bytes should produce red/red/red or otherwise fail the explicit blue Form assertion.

The current shared helper nevertheless maps absent Link /H plus /D to Push, so it bypasses the default-I effect on links. A drafted test states the inferred composition (show /D, then apply default I); parent should resolve this reading before calling a confirmed code defect. Explicit I control passes yellow; absent H differs. The spec supplies no Link counterpart to the widget conflict invoked by ADR0123.

original_decision: Run ECMAScript actions from a trigger chain separately from non-script actions performed by the viewer; leave the relative order between the two kinds unspecified/not preserved.
reason: The chain walker and action reader both preserve their own depth-first order, but their separate consumers do not preserve the relative order Table 196 establishes for a mixed /Next chain. A script can observe the viewer state after a preceding action through the public ScriptEvent.document snapshot. The current `Scripts` level permits that script to execute at on, warn, and answered-ask; off-by-default and process confinement do not establish a blanket permission to reorder supported actions when the runner is supplied. A100/A286 changed the scope premise by making execution required at supplied-runner sites, with no order exception.

test_evidence: Existing action-tree tests assert depth-first ordering among non-script actions; existing script-chain tests assert order among script actions. Neither crosses the two action kinds. The new test draft uses a reversed JavaScript->SetOCGState positive control and a SetOCGState->JavaScript expected-order case. The runner reads `event.document.layers[0].on` through the public API, and final Query::Layers verifies the viewer-side action. Root promoted and ran the test: ordering assertion fails after the reverse-order and final-state controls pass.

Later ADRs 1750/1752 connected runner dispatch to interactive events; ADR 1904 added the outline action site; A100/A286 established that a supplied runner executes supported scripts in this document/viewer. These successors retained the separate-dispatch design but did not amend Table 196's ordering rule.

The script request path should remain, while dispatch is qualified to retain the enclosing /Next sequence relative to actions performed by the viewer.

reason: Per-window event delivery and suppressing a refusal for a script that ran remain correct. The order contract applies within the public viewer and cannot be resolved by saying the two paths are both called.

original_decision: Raise PV together with PO for the current page and PI together with PC for the page left, because the then-current viewer showed one page at a time.
reason: ADR 0164's one-page factual premise became stale when ADR 0441 built OneColumn, TwoColumnLeft/Right, and TwoPageLeft/Right layouts and ADR 0442 delivered those arrangements through the remaining host. ADRs 1750 and 1752 later made a separate, explicit policy choice that PV/PI follow the focused page and neighbors in a continuous layout receive neither. The current behavior is therefore a documented limitation, not an unnoticed implementation regression; it remains a reachable departure from Table 197 and needs the successor policy reviewed against the effective spec.
current_code_evidence: crates/viewer-core/src/layout.rs::place produces the visible page placements; viewer/layout.rs::arrange stores them in open.on_screen. navigation.rs::page_events ignores that set and enumerates annotations only for the old open.page_index and new open.page_index. Query::PageGeometry is based on open.on_screen and interpreted state, providing a public observable for the actual shown set.
test_evidence: Existing `crates/viewer-core/tests/headless.rs::table_29s_two_page_left_shows_exactly_two_pages_side_by_side` asserts two-page placement but no trigger effects. Draft tests `newly_visible_neighbor_gets_pv_before_it_becomes_current` and `page_remaining_visible_does_not_get_pi_when_current_page_changes` use complete exact-xref PDFs and URI action effects, and separately assert the visible geometry/current-page distinction. Root executed both tests: the PV and PI assertions fail after the independent controls pass.
spec_or_external_sources: Effective EC3 §12.6.3 text and Table 197 distinguish page-open from page-visible events; §7.7.2 Table 29 defines multi-page layouts. ADR 0441 and 0442 are the direct successor implementation records establishing the changed premise and current host support.
changed_premise: The viewer is no longer single-page only. ADR 0441 implemented all six arrangements in viewer-core and two hosts; ADR 0442 completed the tier-2 host. Later ADRs deliberately retained focused-page PV/PI semantics despite those layouts.

original_decision: Suppress recursively generated page-event cascades with a one-level raising guard so a page-trigger action cannot walk through an unbounded document.
reason: The recursion guard is a deliberate event-loop policy and remains distinct from the now-invalid coalescing of open and visible events. §12.6.3 states no cascade bound, so the guard should be described as this reader's bounded behavior rather than as a rule derived from the clause. The visibility regression does not require revisiting the guard itself.

remaining_work: Document the recursion guard as a deliberate reader policy. Test it if event dispatch is changed while implementing visible-set transitions.

original_decision: Have page scripts run with the page-open/page-close transition; treat PV/PI as following the page shown, with continuous-layout neighbors receiving neither.
reason: Script runner ownership and separation of script dispatch from non-script actions remain sound. ADR 1750 explicitly chose to make PV/PI follow the shown/current page and acknowledged that continuous-layout neighbors receive neither, despite noting the standard's multi-page-visible distinction. ADR 0441 had already made such layouts reachable. This is a knowingly documented behavior limitation rather than an unnoticed regression, but the visible-set tests prove that the limitation affects actual supported views and Table 197's conditions support revisiting it. The reader's Scripts-off policy does not remove non-script action forms from this requirement.

test_evidence: Existing script hook test asserts OPV and then PC/PI/C for a single page turn; it has no multi-page layout or visibility-set assertion. The new draft uses URI actions to avoid conflating trigger timing with script runner policy.

original_decision: Raise PV and PI alongside current-page turns in every window; continuous-layout neighboring pages raise neither.

The supported layouts can place multiple pages at once, so this is a known and exercised-by-layout behavior limitation rather than an accidental omission. Table 197 ties those events to visibility, making the explicit policy a departure worth reconsidering. Keep the separate host/script runner boundary; the disputed unit is event selection.

original_decision: A referenced form, tiling pattern or annotation appearance that states no Resources is assigned the page dictionary the reader used, on the premise that §7.8.3 ends the lookup at the page and assignment changes no name resolution.
reason: The page fallback is not effective for patterns. Table 74 requires pattern Resources; the missing-entry reader route uses an empty dictionary, and neither §7.8.3 nor EC3 Issue #128 states a pattern fallback. The archive assignment is nevertheless reachable and writes the page dictionary into a referenced pattern lacking Resources, which can make a page-only XObject name resolve and add marks. ADR 2500's blanket unchanged-resolution assertion is therefore false for malformed pattern inputs. This does not imply ISO requires a reader to reject or repair the malformed source.
current_code_evidence: pdf-archive/survey/patterns.rs::Walk::pattern reads absent pattern Resources as empty and records the stream with own_resources=false. pdf-transform/archive/reader_resources.rs::assign accepts every referenced opened object with own_resources=false and files Edit::Assign(page resources), without discriminating patterns. archive/rewrite/reader_resources.rs::give_reader_resources inserts that value when the stream dictionary lacks Resources. The pass is prepared from the explicit-resource finding in prepare.rs.
test_evidence: The PDF/A-archive survey fixture `tiling-pattern-without-resources.pdf` has a pattern cell using /Sq while only the page defines /Sq; its test asserts that the pattern's /Sq remains missing. pdf-model has an equivalent assertion. Draft paired observation adds (1) a valid pattern that explicitly maps /Sq and must render equivalently before/after, then (2) the malformed counterpart whose source reports missing /Sq and whose converted output may draw the page-defined /Sq form.

decision_id: ADR 0191 §§2–3: render Popup as host window; activate linked popup from markup or Popup object; opening/closing lifecycle
original_decision: Read Popup dictionaries in pdf-model, route them through viewer-core as window state, and draw them in host chrome because §12.5.6.14 prohibits a Popup appearance stream. Activation of an annotation with a linked window exhibits it; this product closes on a subsequent activation.
reason: No-page-appearance/host-window separation remains coherent and new positive-parent/no-popup-page-mark test passes. Parent source-based interpretation of12.5.1 plus Stamp12.5.6.12 exposes a supplied-note activation gap when optional Popup absent; this is independent of need to synthesize a PDF annotation object. Second-click close remains product choice.
current_code_evidence: `popup_of` resolves the markup's /Popup or group/thread window. `activate_object` toggles it if present; `has_a_window` also includes Text. `toggle_popup` looks up a matching Popup in `popups` and returns false if none exists. `popups` synthesizes a window for standalone Text without /Popup, but not other markups.
test_evidence: Complete-PDF public tests `a_document_that_opens_a_popup_window_says_so_before_anybody_clicks`, `a_closed_popup_is_no_window_until_the_annotation_is_clicked`, and `a_host_may_open_a_popup_without_a_pointer` cover linked Popup behavior. `a_text_note_with_no_popup_is_opened_and_closed_by_its_activation` covers the specific Text clause. No public test establishes behavior for Square/Highlight without /Popup.

remaining_work: Address supplied-note Stamp activation separately; broader subtype matrix remains partial.
parent_review: Selected ADR unit/source/assertions read; no whole-document certification.

decision_id: ADR 0294 §1: Text /Open and Popup /Open are independent opening conditions
original_decision: Read both Table 175 Text /Open and Table 186 Popup /Open as conditions that can open the same Text popup; neither is a close instruction, so the initial opening result is their disjunction.
reason: Current `opens_with_the_page` does this, and the test inventory includes the distinct Text-own-window case. The selected ADR claim is specific to Text annotations: only Table 175 gives a separate annotation-level /Open that says a Text annotation opens a window. It should not be generalized to Line/Square/Markup annotations whose clauses say 'when opened' without giving them a Table 175 entry. Table 186 /Open remains the Popup's explicit initial state for linked windows.
current_code_evidence: `opens_with_the_page` first checks the Popup dictionary's Table 186 /Open, then checks a parent of subtype Text and obtains the grouped primary's Table 175 /Open. It does not check arbitrary markup /Open keys.

remaining_work: No new gap in Text/Popup initial Open disjunction. Activation without link is a separate behavior and Stamp now has a reproduced regression.
parent_review: Selected ADR unit/source/assertions read; no whole-document certification.

original_decision: Treat Table 171's Markup column as the parent subtype set, excluding Sound because §12.5.6.2 expressly says Sound has no popup; do not infer that FreeText or Projection are excluded from the broad parent relationship.
reason: The selected conclusion follows direct normative definitions: §12.5.6.14 says a Popup is associated with a markup parent; Table 172 applies to all markup annotations; Table 171 identifies the classification; Sound's clause in §12.5.6.2 expressly states no popup. This is separate from whether an optional /Popup reference's absence requires synthetic UI.

decision_id: ADR 1721 §2: script-visible text edits apply only to Text notes, other annotation Contents refused
original_decision: Treat a Text note's contents as a reader edit through ViewState and popup windows; refuse script edits to other annotation subtype Contents and grouped subordinates.
reason: The script-side choice is internally explicit and follows the acknowledged API surface; it should not be described as a settled ISO exclusion. No owner scope ratification specifically excludes editing existing non-Text annotation Contents, and CLAUDE.md's closed-scope rule means an unratified exclusion cannot be inferred. Conversely, §12.5.6.14's `shall be used for editing the parent's text` describes a Popup annotation's purpose and does not expressly define processor editing capabilities for every markup subtype; Table 172 makes a Popup link optional. The evidence supports a product-policy boundary with an unresolved standards reading, not a proven conformance violation. Parent distinguishes proven product limitation from a blanket ISO processor verdict: the valid supplied Square popup exists, so optional-link absence cannot justify inability to edit it. Literal editing requirement remains unfulfilled as a capability, and no owner exclusion was found.
current_code_evidence: `popup::retypable` recognizes only Text; viewer editing rejects SetNoteText for a Square parent, while popup display still shows the Square's Contents. The script annotations path likewise routes Contents through set_note_text.
test_evidence: `a_window_whose_text_is_not_a_note_s_offers_no_retyping_and_refuses_one` explicitly asserts the Square behavior. ADR 1721 cites `each_annotation_is_told_where_table_167_lets_it_go`, `a_script_retypes_a_text_note_and_its_window_shows_it`, and `a_group_s_subordinate_note_is_not_retyped`. The cited tests establish the selected API policy, not an ISO-required subtype matrix.
changed_premise: ADR 1721's own script API scope does not answer whether the Popup annotation's `shall` language obliges a general interactive processor to expose non-Text parent text for editing. No direct ratification for that distinction was found.
remaining_work: Separate follow-up should settle broader existing-annotation note editing and reconcile completion evidence; no new permission request or production change is required for recording this limitation.
parent_review: Selected ADR unit/source/assertions read; no whole-document certification.

decision_id: ADR 1726 §2: popup editing is limited to Text note windows
original_decision: Make window editing available only for the subtype Text; other markup windows display their Contents but have no keyboard, and SetNoteText for them is reported and not logged.
reason: This is the current product's demonstrated and tested capability boundary, but it is not backed by an explicit owner ratification excluding non-Text markup editing. The code intentionally shows a Square popup's Contents, rejects edits naming that Square, and the public test asserts the refusal. §12.5.6.14 says a Popup shall be used for editing its parent's text, while Table172 makes the Popup link optional. The clause's imperative may describe producer/object purpose or require reader editing capability; the current audit cannot resolve that grammatical/scope question. Mark the ledger's `implemented` claim as insufficient evidence of the full literal feature until that question is adjudicated. Parent distinguishes proven product limitation from a blanket ISO processor verdict: the valid supplied Square popup exists, so optional-link absence cannot justify inability to edit it. original_decision: Accept multi-page stale reprojection when page-derived placement transforms differ by at most half a device pixel, claiming that this keeps every feature in the same pixel; this bound is the display grid's own quantisation and is separated empirically from ordinary-scroll residuals and zoom rearrangements.
reason: A maximum displacement bound is a useful, measured-in-device-units approximation policy for deciding whether to reuse one placement across a column. The mathematical inference that any displacement below 0.5 necessarily preserves each feature's pixel cell is false without a phase assumption: a point arbitrarily near a pixel boundary can cross it under an arbitrarily small displacement. The actual sampler is filtered, so pixel values also change continuously with subpixel phase. In addition, one_placement measures pre-snap disagreement, then snaps a pure translation by up to 0.5 per axis; the reported `within` is not the total error of the returned transform relative to every page. Keep 0.5 as an intentional threshold on inter-page transform disagreement, but do not describe it as same-cell identity, unchanged raster features, or a final-placement error bound. Empirical scroll/zoom separation supports this chosen threshold for the measured column, not a universal quantization theorem. A point at x=0.49 moved to0.51 crosses a nearest-sample cell boundary with only0.02 displacement. Independently rounded x/y translation adds up to sqrt(0.5) displacement; within reports disagreement before that snap, not final output error.

original_decision: Measure the maximum Euclidean difference between two affine placements over the whole rectangular texture by evaluating the four corners; the norm of the affine difference is convex and reaches its maximum at an extreme point.
reason: For an affine displacement vector d(p), the norm ||d(p)|| is convex. Every point in a rectangle is a convex combination of its vertices, so convexity bounds its value by the largest vertex value. The implementation's four-corner maximum is therefore exact in real arithmetic for the declared rectangle; this argument is separate from the invalid implication that a <0.5 displacement preserves pixel membership. `TargetSpec` dimensions are bounded by 2^24 and exactly representable in f32, though transform evaluation remains floating-point arithmetic.

It does not expressly require readers to alter a substitute outline to match dictionary metrics. The ADR's other premise—that an effective Table 109 sentence permits explicit Widths to override a standard-14 font—is withdrawn: EC3 #47/#48 strikes the all-four/override paragraph. Treat the scaling as an implementation policy for layout fidelity, not as a direct SHALL. The ADR also quotes a processor SHALL from §9.6.2.1 that EC3 retires; the current metric fallback remains useful but is no longer required by that sentence. Parent additionally distinguishes advance width from ink bounds: glyph overhang can extend beyond an advance. The current comment claiming displacement bounds ink from above is not generally valid. Condensing by a bounded median remains a heuristic; the unit test proves horizontal scaling and unchanged height, not an ISO requirement to fit all ink within each advance.

original_decision: Construct all four named marks from QuadPoints, derive thickness and wave dimensions from quad height, multiply Highlight, and use lower page-y midpoint to decide which edge is the bottom.
reason: Actual Figure84 agrees with CCW prose and shows x1/x2 as baseline edge, contrary to ADR/source claim that they are the top. Absolute page-y choice paints an overline for rotated valid text. Height-relative thickness/wavelength remain choices; they do not justify choosing the wrong side. Quad also reconstructs a parallelogram from three corners, losing a valid trapezoid far vertex.

remaining_work: Separate production fix should preserve the complete quadrilateral and baseline-relative mark placement, with deliberate malformed-order recovery distinct from normative valid inputs.

reason: Keep the backend stroke expansion/alpha-mask boundary. Existing path-stroke assertions distinguish outline marks/gaps/outside area. Root added a stronger glyph-stroke gap regression because the old red/no-green test could accept a solid-red fallback. All five new tiling tests pass.
